title: Which water can I use?
summary: A table of water sources and the treatment each one needs. Some can't be made safe.

blocks.text: Pick the safest source you have. **Bottled water first.** Then stored tap water. Then water from the house (water heater, melted ice). Outdoor water is last.

blocks.alt: Which water can I drink. Safest first: bottled, then stored tap, then house water, outdoor water last. Do not drink: flood water, radiator or boiler water, tap water under a do-not-drink advisory, water that smells of fuel or has a sheen, or pool and spa water. Treat first, then drink: tap water under a boil-water advisory (rolling boil for 1 minute), creek, river, pond or lake water, rainwater as a last resort, and a flooded private well after disinfection and testing. Treat in this order: settle and strain, filter if you have a portable filter, then boil for 1 minute or use bleach for 30 minutes or tablets by the label.
blocks.caption: Which sources you can drink, which you can't, and how to treat the rest.

rows: Rolling boil 1 minute, cool. Boil filtered water too.
Boiling does not fix chemicals. Use bottled water.
CDC says it can be made safe by treatment. FEMA lists collected rainwater among water not to drink. Strain it, then boil or disinfect.
Can carry livestock waste, sewage and chemicals. Let it settle or strain it, then filter and boil or disinfect.
Same as above. EPA says flowing water is generally better than still water.
Don't drink it, wash with it or wade in it. It carries germs, waste, chemicals, and may be electrified.

Never use water from a heating system.
Disinfect, test it, and call the health department.

blocks.text: **Chemicals and fuel can't be filtered or boiled out.** If water smells of fuel, has a sheen, or may carry toxic chemicals or radioactive material, don't drink it and don't treat it. Boiling and bleach kill germs, not chemicals. Portable filters like the ones in the filter guide don't remove chemicals either, and they aren't made for water near large farm operations or industrial ponds.

items: Water with floating material, a dark color or a questionable odor.
Don't use unsafe water to make ice, mix baby formula, wash dishes or brush teeth.
Let cloudy water settle. Strain it through a cloth, paper towel or coffee filter.
If you have a portable filter, filter it (see the filter guide).
Then **boil** it for 1 minute, or add **bleach** (30 minutes) or **tablets** (follow the label).
